layers.name: Controller / API Layer
layers.description: Spring @RestController classes and HTTP endpoint definitions that receive requests, validate input, and delegate to the application service layer. Includes websocket endpoints.

layers.name: Application Service Layer
layers.description: Orchestrates use-cases via DDD application services (*AppService / *AppServiceImpl) and traditional service classes (*Service / *ServiceImpl). Coordinates domain operations, manages transactions, and converts between DTOs and domain models.

layers.name: Domain Layer
layers.description: DDD domain elements: entities, value objects, aggregate roots, enums, and repository interfaces. Pure business rules with no external dependencies.

layers.name: Persistence / Repository Layer
layers.description: Data access: MyBatis-Plus Mapper interfaces, MyBatis XML mappers, and SQL DDL/schema files. Implements repository abstractions and owns all database interaction.

layers.name: Infrastructure / Cross-cutting
layers.description: Cross-cutting concerns: Spring configuration classes, AOP aspects, interceptors, scheduled jobs (Quartz), Redis services, OSS upload providers, login providers, websocket handlers, and the yf-ability cross-cutting module.

layers.name: Shared / Common
layers.description: Base DTOs, base controllers, exception handling, AOP aspects, annotations, API response wrappers, and core utilities shared across all modules. Includes the yf-core and wk-general modules.

layers.name: System / Platform
layers.description: System management modules: user, role, menu, department, dictionary, notice, and operation log. The admin-facing foundation of the platform (yf-module-system).

layers.name: Wiki Documentation
layers.description: Project wiki and rule documentation under .qoder/repowiki, .qoder/rules, .qoder/skills, and module-level README files.

layers.name: Configuration & Build
layers.description: Build and deployment configuration: Maven pom.xml, Spring application*.yml, Dockerfile, run scripts, SQL migration files, and intermediate workspace files.

layers.name: Residual / Misc
layers.description: Files that did not match a primary layer pattern; typically tail batches or special-case types.

tour.title: Entry Point & Bootstrap
tour.description: The Spring Boot application bootstraps from the yf-web module (WebApplication.java) which composes all yf-modules and wk-modules into a single deployable JAR. The yf-web module owns the executable entry point and central web wiring, while the wk-modules contribute feature bundles via Spring auto-discovery.
tour.languageLesson: In Spring Boot, the @SpringBootApplication class is intentionally minimal: it sits on top of the assembled graph. Configuration is delegated to @Configuration classes — controllers and services are auto-discovered via classpath scanning, so adding a new module only requires dropping a jar on the classpath.

tour.title: Web & Cross-cutting Config
tour.description: The yf-web/config package wires HTTP-level concerns: CORS for the Vue frontends, MyBatis-Plus pagination, Web MVC converters, WebSocket, Jackson serialization, and Swagger. The yf-ability/config package carries reusable infrastructure beans (Quartz, Redis, AI chat configs) that any module can inject.
tour.languageLesson: Notice the separation: yf-web/config is web transport (HTTP/WebSocket/MVC), while yf-ability/config is reusable infrastructure (scheduling, cache, AI). The cross-cutting AOP filters — DataDictFilter, DataPermissionHandler, FillMetaObjectHandler — are all declared in yf-web/aspect and intercept requests/queries uniformly.

tour.title: Shiro Security & JWT
tour.description: Authentication and authorization use Apache Shiro backed by a JWT token filter. MyShiroRealm loads the user's roles/permissions, ShiroConfig defines the filter chain and stateless session policy, and JwtUtils handles token generation/validation. JwtFilter parses the Authorization header on every request and binds the principal to the security context.
tour.languageLesson: Stateless Shiro + JWT is a common Spring pattern: the realm is invoked only on first access (token refresh), and the filter chain is configured to be stateless so session replication is unnecessary. @RequiresPermissions annotations on service methods are enforced through AOP, decoupling authorization from controller code.

tour.title: Core API & DTOs
tour.description: yf-core defines the universal API contract shared by every module: ApiRest is the uniform response wrapper (code/message/data), ApiError enumerates standard error codes, BaseController exposes common helpers (current user, paging), and PagingReqDTO/PageResult standardize list pagination requests and responses.
tour.languageLesson: A typed Result<T> envelope pays for itself: controllers can return Result.ok() / Result.fail(code, msg) and clients always know the shape. The @Dict annotation here is a custom meta-annotation that the DataDictFilter AOP interceptor reads to auto-translate dictionary codes to human labels at serialization time.

tour.title: Exception Handling & AOP
tour.description: Centralized error handling: ServiceException is the runtime business exception, and ServiceExceptionHandler in yf-web converts it (and validation errors) into a uniform ApiRest JSON response. Cross-cutting aspects — LogInject for audit logging, DataProtect for field-level desensitization, and MyBatis-Plus meta-object fillers for createdBy/updatedBy — all live in the aspect packages.
tour.languageLesson: Spring's @RestControllerAdvice + @ExceptionHandler lets you centralize error-to-HTTP mapping in one place — the alternative (try/catch in every controller) scatters concerns. Combined with @Around AOP for logging and the MyBatis-Plus MetaObjectHandler interface for audit columns, you get cross-cutting behavior without polluting domain code.

tour.title: Ability / Infrastructure Modules
tour.description: yf-ability is a bag of pluggable capabilities used across modules: Excel import/export, face recognition (Aliyun), upload providers (local/COS/OSS), Redis facade, social logins (WeChat, Corp WeChat), live streaming, plan events, office document conversion, and IP geolocation. Each capability exposes a config DTO and a service that any module can @Autowired.
tour.languageLesson: The Factory pattern is used heavily here (UploadFactory, FaceFactory) so providers can be swapped via Spring configuration without touching call sites. Look at the /providers subpackage of upload and face to see how each implementation (Aliyun, Tencent, Local) is structured identically — that's the Strategy pattern in disguise.

tour.title: System Module
tour.description: yf-module-system holds the platform's identity & access control surface: user, role, menu, department, dictionary, notice, login, log, key-point knowledge, enterprise, and group management. Each feature exposes a /admin controller and matching service/mapper triad under com.yf.system.modules.<feature>.
tour.languageLesson: All system features share the same package layout: <feature>/{controller,service,dto,entity,mapper}. This is a deliberate convention over configuration — once you know one feature, you know all of them. The service interface is intentionally thin (CRUD + business queries) and the heavy lifting happens inside MyBatis-Plus lambda queries.

tour.title: Course Module
tour.description: yf-module-course delivers the learner experience: course catalog (Course, CourseFile), learning progress (CourseLearn), Q&A and comments, and a recommendation engine. It splits into /admin (operator-side CRUD) and /client (learner-facing APIs), reflecting the typical split for content management vs consumption.
tour.languageLesson: The /admin vs /client split is a common multi-tenant pattern: admin controllers trust an authenticated operator with broad permissions, while client controllers are scoped to the calling user (often via Shiro's @RequiresUser + custom data-scope filters). Keeping them in separate packages prevents accidental cross-exposure of operator-only endpoints.

tour.title: Exam Module
tour.description: yf-module-exam is the largest module and the heart of the platform: exam authoring (admin/exam, admin/paper, admin/tmpl templates), exam taking (client/exam), review workflows (admin/review), live proctoring (admin/watch + websocket endpoints), and face-based identity verification (client/face). Each subdomain is its own controller tree.
tour.languageLesson: WebSocket endpoints sit alongside REST controllers because they share the same authentication filter chain (the JwtFilter runs on the HTTP upgrade request). The watch/proctor feature shows how a single business concept (proctoring) is decomposed into REST control plane (admin/watch/*) and WebSocket data plane (ExamEndpoint) — a clean separation when real-time events matter.

tour.title: Repo (Question Bank) Module
tour.description: yf-module-repo manages the question bank: Qu (questions), QuAnswer (options/correct answers), QuGen (auto-generation), QuReport (user reports), Repo (repository metadata), and RepoTrain (training/answering sessions). Both /admin (CRUD by operators) and /client (student training) views are provided.
tour.languageLesson: Question banks are deceptively complex: a single 'question' may have multiple types (single choice, multi-choice, fill-blank, essay), each with different answer storage shapes. The codebase encodes this through a QuType enum and per-type answer DTOs (QuAnswerDTO) — a discriminated union pattern implemented with Java inheritance rather than a sealed type.

tour.title: Plan, Training & Stat Modules
tour.description: Three supporting modules close the learning loop: yf-module-plan builds org-level learning plans (NodeController, PlanUserController), yf-module-training-plan manages enterprise-wide annual training plan collections, and yf-module-stat produces statistics/reports consumed by admin dashboards (StatRepoController, StatTotalExamController).
tour.languageLesson: Statistics modules typically read-heavy: services here are mostly composed of MyBatis aggregate queries (count, sum, group by) and rarely write. The StatTotalExamController is a good example of an 'analytics endpoint' pattern — the controller accepts date-range and dimension parameters, then the service runs a single targeted SQL with proper indexing.

tour.title: WK Modules (DDD-style)
tour.description: wk-modules follow an explicit DDD port/adapter layout with three top-level packages per module: application (use cases / CQRS command-query split), domain (pure entities and factories, no Spring annotations), and infrastructure (JPA/MyBatis adapters, external service clients). Compared to the yf-modules which use a flat controller/service/mapper structure, wk-modules enforce stronger layering.
tour.languageLesson: The 'AppOpService' / 'AppQueryService' split is a lightweight form of CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation): write operations and read operations live in different interfaces, allowing independent optimization and clearer intent. The domain/ package is deliberately free of Spring and JPA imports — those concerns live only in infra/.

tour.title: Quartz Jobs & Scheduling
tour.description: yf-job is the dedicated scheduling module: JobService manages Quartz triggers and groups, and the yf-modules each register jobs under their own /job subpackage. JobGroup and JobPrefix enums keep trigger names namespaced across modules so cron collisions are impossible.
tour.languageLesson: Quartz in Spring is most cleanly used with @PersistJobDataAfterExecution and @DisallowConcurrentExecution on the job class, plus a database-backed JobStore for clustering. The JobPrefix/JobGroup enums here enforce a naming convention that prevents one module from accidentally clobbering another's scheduled task.

tour.title: Persistence & SQL DDL
tour.description: The sql/ directory and the el_* table nodes are the ground truth for the data model. el_ is the table prefix and snake_case naming is used throughout. DatabaseMigrationRunner and KgLegacyMigrationRunner in yf-web apply migrations on application start, so a fresh deploy boots into a usable schema.
tour.languageLesson: el_ is the project-wide table prefix; combined with snake_case, every column is globally unique without a schema per module. The 'Knowledge Graph' (kg) tables (el_sys_key_point, el_sys_key_point_edge) hint at a future graph-store feature — a separate DataSourceConfig is already wired so graph reads can route to a different store than transactional writes.
